claim: Full-scale pressure of the 0 to 10 m range is 98.07 kPa (PR-001)
law: Hydrostatic pressure p = rho g h

claim: A vented (gauge) transducer cancels air pressure swings that would put +/-306 mm on an absolute sensor (+/-3 kPa weather)
law: Gauge pressure is referenced to the atmosphere through the vent capillary (USGS TM 1-A1, 2011)

claim: ADC step (quantisation) 0.52 mm with a 150 ohm shunt and a 16-bit ADC (PR-003); noise-limited resolution of the probe and ADC is to measure at TRL 4
law: 16 mA x 150 ohm = 2.4 V span over a 125 uV step [A2]

claim: With the 24 V boost the transducer gets 20.16 V at 22 mA through 63 m of cable (the 12 V rail alone gives 7.56 V)
law: Ohm's law round the loop; transducer minimum 12 V (BOM line 1) [B1]

claim: At a 25 mA fault the shunt gives 3.75 V; a 10 kohm series resistor keeps the ADC input current to 15 uA
law: ADS1115 absolute maximum: input current 10 mA continuous, VDD + 0.3 V [B1b]

claim: Sensor energy 38.2 mWh a day at 15 min, 5 % or less of FieldNode's 100 mW sensor allowance (PR-008)
law: Energy balance: 24 V x 22 mA x 2 s through boost (85 %) and rail (90 %) plus the controller [B2, B3]

claim: A 0.25 % class probe reaches +/-20 mm after calibration (PR-004). First run: a two-point calibration with a 1 m lift was claimed to fix span; two tape readings and two repeatability terms over 1 m give 1.5 % of span, 148 mm at 10 m: fails (independent review). Fixed: offset from the installation tape reading, span from the probe's per-unit factory certificate (0.10 % of reading, to confirm), refined by tape checks at levels 3 m or more apart
law: Error budget of eight independent terms, root sum square against worst-case sum [C3, C4, C4b]
check: RSS 16.0 mm, worst case 37.1 mm against 20 mm; terms are typical datasheet values, not measured

claim: Water density changes 0.29 % between 4 and 25 degC, so firmware uses a fixed site density set at installation
law: Thiesen equation of state for water [C2]

claim: Using standard gravity reads 10 m about 27 mm low at the equator; firmware uses local gravity
law: WGS 84 normal gravity formula [C1]

claim: A quarterly tape check keeps the uncorrected drift to 5 mm or less if the probe drifts 20 mm a year or less (PR-005)
law: Drift budget: 20 mm a year over a 91-day interval [C8]
check: 5 mm between checks against the 20 mm target; long-term drift of low-cost vented transducers is not published

claim: Cable and probe hanging 60 m in air (35 N) stay below the 400 N strain member (PR-002)
law: Weight of 0.055 kg/m cable and a 0.25 kg probe [D3]

claim: Cable stretch at 60 m (16 mm) is a fixed offset the installation calibration removes; a full 10 m level swing changes it by 2.7 mm (aramid strain member taken as about 1 mm2 at 70 GPa, EA 70 kN, typical, to confirm with the cable maker)
law: Elongation = integral of tension over EA; buoyancy of the submerged cable

claim: The 60 m access tube hanging dry (264 N, 0.82 MPa) stays well below PVC's 48 MPa tensile strength
law: Self-weight stress of PVC, 1,400 kg/m3 [D4]

claim: The tube string is held at the plate over its life. Friction of the split collar alone: 833 N new, about 278 N after PVC creep, against 792 N (3 x 264 N): fails. Fixed with a 5 mm stainless clevis pin through the tube on a chord above the collar, carrying 299 N (tube, cable and probe): sustained PVC bearing 7.0 MPa on the 4.3 mm chord wall against PVC's 13.8 MPa long-term design stress, pin shear 7.6 MPa; 69 mm of tube above the pin rules out shear-out
law: Clamp preload F = T/(K d); friction mu F; PVC stress relaxation; pin bearing against the long-term design stress of PVC 1120 (13.8 MPa, 2,000 psi)

claim: The collar spreads the tube load onto the HDPE seal plate at 0.24 MPa
law: Bearing stress against about 20 MPa for HDPE [D5]

claim: The probe and padlock hang from the M5 eye bolt; the PVC cap walls carry 0.81 MPa in bearing
law: Bearing on two cap walls against about 50 MPa for PVC [D6, D7]

claim: The service loop in the junction box (1.13 m) lets the probe lift 1 m for the response check at installation and be pulled for inspection
law: Coil length 2 pi r n from the model

claim: A 22 mm probe runs freely in the tube: 2.3 mm radial at the nominal bore, 1.74 mm at the thickest Sch 40 wall and 1.24 mm at a solvent-weld joint with a 0.5 mm cement bead, below the 2 mm design rule: fails. Fixed by wiping the joints and pulling a 23 mm drift through the string before the probe goes in, which proves at least 0.5 mm radial everywhere, ovality and bow included; 0.5 mm is enough for a probe hanging free on its cable (nominal-wall bore 26.1 mm gives 2.07 mm)
law: Pipe bore from OD and wall tolerances (ASTM D1785); running clearance

claim: The 40 drilled 8 mm holes (2011 mm2) let the water in the tube follow the casing level: the tube's air vents through the cap's conduit to the box breather, and even at 10 mm of head difference the tube fills 10 m in about 10 s
law: Open area against the bore area; orifice flow
check: 3.6 x bore area >= 1 x bore area

claim: 10 g of silica gel keeps the vent and box air dry about 552 days at worst-case daily breathing, more than the 91-day change interval (PR-017); permeation through gaskets and glands is not counted
law: Gas law breathing at a 30 K daily swing; silica gel uptake 20 % by mass [F1]

claim: At 55 degC ambient in full sun the junction box stays within the 85 degC rating of the modules (PR-015)
law: Solar gain alpha G A_sun against convection h A_total, alpha 0.5, G 1,000 W/m2, h 10 W/m2K, A_sun/A_total 0.22
check: 66 degC by the balance; small enclosures in full sun are often measured 20 to 35 K above ambient, which would reach 75 to 90 degC

claim: One year of 15 min readings fills 1.12 MB of FieldNode's 16 MB flash (PR-007)
law: 35,040 readings x 32 bytes [E1]

claim: Pumping-test batches every 30 min on a public network use 22.7 s of airtime a day at SF9 (PR-006); valid at SF9 only: at SF10 and above a test sends from a private gateway or in hourly batches
law: Semtech LoRa time-on-air formula; 30 s a day fair use on The Things Network [E4]

claim: 316 stainless, PVC, HDPE, EPDM and PU or PE cable jackets can be had in grades certified for drinking water contact (PR-009)
law: NSF/ANSI/CAN 61 lists components of all these material classes
check: Material classes are routinely certified; no certificate is in hand for the chosen low-cost parts, so PR-009 stays not met on evidence

claim: Disinfecting the probe, cable and tube with chlorine solution before they go into the well reduces the risk of bringing bacteria into the supply
law: AWWA C654 (disinfection of wells) and the local water authority's practice
check: Standard well practice; the build plan and PRC safety notes carry it

claim: Two people can lower the 30 m design-case tube string and cable (15 kg) by hand; at 60 m (30 kg) a third person or a hand line is used
law: UK HSE guideline weights, 16 kg per person (women) to 25 kg (men) for lifting close to the body (INDG143)
check: 7.6 kg per person <= 16 kg per person

claim: Every WellSense circuit runs at 24 V DC or less, within extra-low voltage (PR-018)
law: ELV band: 120 V ripple-free DC or less (IEC 61140)

claim: A short between the cable cores puts the 24 V boost across the shunt: 149 mA and 3.3 W in a small shunt: fails. Fixed with a 50 mA resettable fuse (PTC) in series with the loop on the interface board: it trips within about 1 s, and a 0.6 W metal film shunt carries 3.3 W for that second; normal loop current (22 mA) is below its hold current
law: Ohm's law; PTC hold and trip currents; short-time overload of film resistors

claim: Option B: back-pressure equals the head over the orifice plus the weight of the air column (71 mm at 30 m), which firmware corrects
law: Hydrostatics of water and of the compressed air column, ideal gas

claim: Option B: the bubble-forming overpressure at a 4 mm orifice is about 7 mm; when the pump stops a pinned meniscus leaves 0 to 7 mm, carried as 2 mm in B7
law: Laplace pressure 2 sigma / r, sigma 0.072 N/m

claim: Option B: pump 1.2 W for 8 s and the controller 10 s per reading, 263 mWh a day at 15 min, within FieldNode's 2.4 Wh sensor allowance (11.0 % of 100 mW, above the 5 % target of PR-008)
law: Energy balance

claim: Option B: a 12 V miniature diaphragm pump reaches the 118 kPa needed (full head plus 20 %)
law: Pump maker's pressure curve
check: To assess at part selection; many small pumps stop near 80 kPa

claim: Option B: the 33 m line holds 475 mL; the first fill at full head needs about 935 mL of free air, a few minutes at 0.3 L/min
law: Boyle's law

claim: Option B: a desiccant inlet keeps compressed air from condensing in the line inside the cooler well; 10 g of gel lasts only about 22 days, so a quarterly change needs about 40 g
law: Dew point of dried air (about -14 degC at line pressure) against groundwater at 15 to 30 degC; gel uptake 20 % by mass
check: Dried inlet air cannot reach saturation in the well; gel sized at 40 g

claim: Option B: a 0 to 150 kPa gauge sensor of the 0.25 % class reaches about 20 mm RSS after calibration (PR-004)
law: Error budget: nonlinearity 0.1 % of 150 kPa, certificate span 10 mm, air column residual 5 mm, tape 3 mm, bubble 2 mm, thermal 4 mm
check: RSS 20 mm against 20 mm; sensor terms typical, not measured

claim: Option C: sampling the echo at 48 kHz gives a 3.6 mm sample spacing; the timing precision of the correlation peak depends on the signal-to-noise ratio (the chirp's own range resolution is about 0.6 m)
law: Time of flight t = 2L/c, c = 343 m/s at 20 degC

claim: Option C: +/-20 mm at 30 m needs the mean air temperature of the column to +/-0.21 K, or reflections from tube joints at known depths to calibrate the speed of sound
law: c proportional to the square root of absolute temperature (0.18 % per K); joint counting as in oil-well echo sounders
check: Whether solvent-weld PVC joints reflect enough is unknown

claim: Option C: at 500 Hz the round trip to water 60 m down loses about 52 dB to the tube walls, recoverable with a short (0.2 s) chirp and correlation once the direct leakage has died away
law: Kirchhoff wall attenuation in a narrow tube
check: 52 dB at 500 Hz over 120 m; holes and joints add loss

claim: Option C: a 1 s chirp and capture at 0.4 W uses 11 mWh a day at 15 min (PR-008)
law: Energy balance

claim: Option C: the speaker and microphone survive the saturated air at the top of the tube
law: Condensation and corrosion of electronics at 100 % relative humidity; IP67 transducers and conformal coating
check: Needs IP67 parts and a coated board; to confirm
